entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

It's done and ready for your test run. Everything is in a separate copy, so the main working tree the other LLM is using was not touched.

**Where:** `D:\Personal_Projects\QuoteCraft-tier1\starter-kit`, on branch `claude/tier1-speed` (pushed, 2 commits). It starts from the proven 100-point package on your current branch.

```bash
atira test-run D:/Personal_Projects/QuoteCraft-tier1/starter-kit --challenge rfq
```

**What changed** (everything traces back to our best scored run, 6:15 / $0.176):

1. **Bid form filled by code from one template.** The clerk spent 25 of its 35 turns (~100 s) choosing one dropdown per turn. Now the model writes the steps for one position once, with placeholders like `{unit_price}`, and code fills in every position in whatever order the form asks.
2. **Parallel agents on the ERP and webmail.** 3 ERP agents and 2 mail agents work in separate tabs of the same logged-in session and split the open questions. The ERP was the slowest site (46 turns one after another).
3. **Click bug fixed.** A click that started a slow page load was reported as failed, then retried and left waiting on a button that no longer existed. That cost 78 s on the login in our best run, and it could press a button twice (a second TAN request voids the first code).
4. **Broken tabs replaced fast.** Short timeouts, and a fresh tab after the first hard failure instead of after two timeouts. This was the other 125 s lost on the flaky tender-portal login.
5. **Cheaper calls.** Each call no longer re-sends the previous page and case file, and the history is shorter, which should roughly halve uncached input.
6. **Smaller speed-ups:**
   - Sites open and log in while the brief is being read.
   - A model call that hangs gets one backup request.
   - Requesting the TAN and asking the mailbox happen in one turn; typing the TAN and finalizing happen in one turn.

**What I verified:**
- 380 unit tests pass (20 new), including a real-browser test that the slow-click bug is fixed.
- A scan of the changes found no values from the public scenario.
- A dry run packs 70 files, 195 KB.

**Not verified yet:** I haven't seen a complete run end to end. My local runs against the practice sites confirmed the click fix, the early login and the parallel agents starting. But the practice model was taking 5–30 s per call and then dropping most calls with 502 errors, so neither run reached the bid form. Your sandbox test run will be the first real test of the template form-fill.

**What to check in the run log:**
- Lines like `[submit] enter_positions: position … entered` for all five positions.
- `more agent(s) on this website`, showing the parallel agents started.
- The final `Total … s` and cost on the `Submission:` line.

If the template form-fill stumbles, send me the run id and I'll fix it from the logs. Each new piece can also be switched off with an environment variable (`ERP_AGENTS=1`, `MAIL_AGENTS=1`, `FULL_TURNS=1`) if one turns out to hurt.

"
The best methods to scrape or handle a website depend on the site's complexity, your coding comfort level, and the scale of the project. [1]
1. By Site Complexity and Technology

* Static HTML Websites (No JavaScript):
   * Best Tools: Python with `requests` and [Beautiful Soup](https://www.upgrad.com/blog/top-final-year-computer-science-projects-topics/).
   * How it works: Pulls the raw HTML directly from the server and parses the tag tree to extract text, links, or tables. It is fast, lightweight, and ideal for blogs or basic directories. [1, 2]
* Dynamic & JavaScript-Heavy Websites (React, Vue, Infinite Scroll):
   * Best Tools: Headless browsers like Playwright, Puppeteer, or Selenium.
   * How it works: Spins up a real (headless) browser engine to execute JavaScript, wait for DOM assembly, and simulate user interactions like scrolling or clicking. [1, 3, 4]
* Large-Scale Crawling & Data Pipelines:
   * Best Tools: [Scrapy](https://scrapy.org/).
   * How it works: A full-fledged Python framework designed for high-speed, asynchronous, multi-page crawling and structured data export.

2. No-Code and AI-Driven Approaches

* Visual Point-and-Click Scrapers:
   * Best Tools: Octoparse or [Browse AI](https://zapier.com/blog/web-scraping/).
   * How it works: You click through a visual browser interface to "train" a robot on what fields or lists to grab, handling pagination and dynamic content automatically. [3, 5]
* AI & Managed Scraping APIs:
   * Best Tools: Firecrawl, ScrapingBee, or Diffbot.
   * How it works: These tools convert unstructured HTML directly into clean markdown or structured JSON using AI schemas, while automatically handling proxy rotation, CAPTCHAs, and anti-bot defenses. [2, 4, 6, 7]

Best Practices for Handling Websites Responsibly

* Check `robots.txt` and Terms of Service: Review the website’s `/robots.txt` file to see which paths are restricted from crawlers.
* Set Rate Limits and Delays: Add a 1 to 3-second delay between requests or limit concurrency so you do not overload the host server.
* Identify Your Bot: Include a custom `User-Agent` header in your requests with a project URL or contact email so site owners know who you are.
* Use Official APIs First: If the website offers a public or commercial JSON/REST API, use it instead of scraping HTML.
* Rotate Proxies: For high-volume or heavily protected sites, use residential or data center proxy pools to prevent IP bans. [1, 4, 8]

content.text:
Partly. We use one of those methods heavily, one in a small way, and most of the rest would get our package rejected under the challenge's fair-play rules.

| Method from that list | Do we use it? | Where |
|---|---|---|
| **Playwright (real browser)** | **Yes, it's our core.** We connect to the 4 sandbox browsers, and every page is read and acted on through Playwright. | `browsers.py`, `browser_env.py` |
| requests + Beautiful Soup (plain HTML) | **A lightweight version, only for downloads.** When the model picks a file (ZIP, CSV, PDF, Word, Excel), `fetch` downloads it with the browser's own session and parses it with Python's built-in HTML parser, `pypdf` and zip/XML readers. | `Tab.fetch`, `document_text` in `browser_env.py` |
| "HTML into structured JSON with AI schemas" (the idea behind Firecrawl and Diffbot) | **The same idea, built ourselves.** Each page an agent files goes to Qwen with a fixed JSON shape (positions, materials, price conditions, mails…) and comes back as typed records. We don't call those services. | `SHAPES` and `_extract` in `casefile.py` |
| LLM driving a browser (the browser-use.com approach in the citations) | **Yes, this is our architecture.** The model sees each page as screen-reader text with numbered controls and decides every click, search and filing. | `worker.py` |
| Scrapy / large-scale crawling | **No, and we must not.** The rules reject "a crawler that collects the websites and hands everything to the model". The model has to choose where to go. | — |
| Firecrawl, ScrapingBee, Diffbot (hosted APIs) | **No, not allowed.** The sandbox can only reach the Atira platform and the four websites, and contacting anything else breaks the rules. | — |
| Octoparse, Browse AI (no-code) | No. Those are trained click paths, which count as "fixed scripts" under the rules. | — |
| Proxy rotation, CAPTCHA bypass services | No. The sandbox has one fixed proxy. The sliders and "I'm not a robot" checks on these sites are part of the challenge, and the model passes them itself. | — |
| robots.txt, rate limits, User-Agent | Not relevant here: these are challenge sites we're required to use, and the agents act at human pace (one action every 1–3 s). | — |

**One idea from the list that could make us faster.** For pages that only need reading, a helper could download the page the model chose directly with the browser's cookies, like `requests`, instead of opening and fully rendering it. File-each record tabs and ERP detail pages are examples. That would skip about 1–2 s of page settling per page. It stays within the rules only while the model picks every address, and it only works on server-rendered pages, so it's a riskier optimisation for the unseen private sites. I'd treat it as a later step after your test run shows how the current changes do.

content.text:
I've read the log, and the agents never actually close and reopen the browsers. Here's what happened.

**Your current run (`run_10def…`) is stuck in a loop on the bid form and won't recover.** Since about 5:00 the clerk has repeated the same action every ~5 s: fill position 01.02's amounts and click "Position hinzufügen". It will keep going until its step cap, close to the 20-minute limit. I'd cancel it. I can do that for you if you say yes, since cancelling needs your confirmation.

## Where the time went

| Phase | Time | What happened |
|---|---|---|
| Investigation | 0:00–3:56 | Bid correct, every question answered. But it took 236 s and cost **$0.31**, against 219 s and $0.14 in our best run. |
| Clerk reaches positions | 3:57–4:24 | Fine, 4 turns. |
| First form-fill template | 4:24–4:40 | Failed at the certification step: the model guessed "Keine", but the option is called "Ohne Zertifizierung". |
| Second template | 4:40–5:01 | Position 01.04 entered. The model then pressed **"Position hinzufügen"** ("add another line"), then "Weiter". |
| Loop | 5:01–now | Position 01.02 shows empty fields again. The model keeps re-filling and pressing "Position hinzufügen", and the page doesn't change. |

**Why the clerk broke.** This is the same trap that zeroed runs d3ca14df and 8a2e1426. The button that saves a position is "Weiter"; "Position hinzufügen" adds a blank extra line and throws the form out of step. My template change made it worse: the model writes the whole template, including the save button, **before** it has seen which button actually saves. So it guessed wrong, and our loop protection didn't stop it.

**Why the investigation got slower and more expensive.** The parallel ERP and mail agents (my change) backfired:
- **Duplicate work:** two or three ERP agents each fetched the same stock and price pages for three of the materials. ERP calls went from 46 to 154, and the run from 155 calls to 364.
- **The main ERP agent looped about 16 times** searching "Hydraulikzylinder" before the requirements were known.
- **The customer-portal agent re-filed the same requirements 12 times.** It thought an extraction was wrong, but the value had correctly been changed by a Q&A amendment.
- **The second mail agent looped about 10 times** on a disabled "next page" button in the archive.
- **Nothing ends the investigation early.** The last open question closed at ~3:34, but it waited until 3:56 for the main ERP agent to finish redundant work.

## Why tabs open and close

We already do what you're suggesting. We connect once to the platform's 4 browsers and keep them for the whole run; moving between pages is just a URL change in the same tab. Opening a browser isn't on our clock, and a new tab costs well under a second. What you saw in the replay were extra tabs:
- the parallel helper agents I added each open their own tab;
- the mailbox agent opens a fresh tab to fetch the TAN;
- a tab is swapped for a fresh one when a page hangs.

None of this is where the time goes: each model call takes ~1.5–3 s, and wasted turns are the cost.

## What I'd change now (in the copy)

1. **Turn the parallel ERP and mail agents off by default.** They doubled the cost without saving time. The code stays, behind a switch.
2. **Clerk:** the model enters the **first** position step by step and sees which button saves it. Only then does it use the template for the remaining positions, built from the steps that worked.
3. **Clerk loop breaker:** after the same actions change nothing three times, code blocks them and tells the model to reload or restart that position.
4. **Template check:** if the form shows the same position again with empty fields after the "save" press, stop at once and report it, rather than counting it as entered.

The other fixes stay (click bug, tab recovery, cheaper history, early login). Should I apply 1–4 now? It's about 15 minutes plus tests, then you can test again.

content.text:
I wouldn't switch to screenshots. They wouldn't fix this failure, and they'd make every turn slower and more expensive. A screenshot does help in one place, and we already use it there.

**Why screenshots wouldn't have helped this run:**
- **The model already saw the page correctly.** Its own words in the loop were "position 01.02 … the amount fields are empty", which is exactly right. The mistake was the decision: it pressed "Position hinzufügen" (add line) instead of "Weiter". A picture of the same page wouldn't tell it which button saves.
- **We already tried a screenshot in this run.** When an agent goes in circles, it gets one turn with full reasoning plus a screenshot. That fired for the clerk at 5:50, and it still chose "Position hinzufügen" again.
- **Text is more precise for forms.** Our page view lists every field and button with its exact label, its value, whether it's disabled, and any error message, each with an id we can click reliably. With screenshots the model has to read pixels and click by coordinates, which goes wrong more often on small dropdowns and buttons.
- **It costs more on every turn.** An image is roughly 1,000–1,500 extra input tokens per call, and the model takes longer to answer. Over ~200 calls that's about +20–30% cost and slower turns, when cost × time is exactly what ranks us.

**Where a screenshot does help:** things the text view can't show, like a slider, a covering overlay, a scanned PDF, or a field that only looks disabled. That's when an agent is stuck, and that's when we already send one.

**What actually fixes the loop** is giving the model the right information at the right moment, plus a hard stop in code:
1. The clerk enters the **first** position step by step, so it sees which button saves a position. The template for the other positions is then built from the steps that worked, not guessed in advance.
2. If the same actions change nothing three times, code **blocks** them and tells the model to reload or restart that position.
3. The template checks that the position actually left the form after the "save" press. If the same position comes back empty, it stops and reports that instead of counting it as entered.
4. The parallel ERP and mail agents go off by default, since they doubled the cost without saving time.

Shall I apply these four now? Also, the current test run is still looping; do you want me to cancel it?

class RepeatedActionsAreRefused(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    """Test run 10def205: the bid clerk filled the same amounts and pressed the same button 40+ times on a page that
    never changed, until its step cap. An agent without an idle hook gets such a repeat refused the third time."""

    async def run_agent(self, idle=None):
        tab = FakeTab(change_on_fill=False)
        fills = []
        original = tab.fill

        async def fill(aid, text, enter=False):
            fills.append(text)
            return await original(aid, text, enter)

        tab.fill = fill
        same = {"thought": "fill it again", "actions": [{"do": "fill", "id": 1, "text": "29"}]}
        replies = [same, same, same, same, {"thought": "other way", "actions": [{"do": "done", "summary": "x"}]}]
        asked = []

        async def model(messages, **kwargs):
            asked.append(messages[-1]["content"])
            return replies.pop(0)

        with patch.object(llm, "chat_json", model):
            await Agent("submit", tab, "system", lambda: "job", max_steps=6, idle=idle).run()
        return fills, asked

    async def test_the_third_identical_turn_is_not_run(self):
        fills, asked = await self.run_agent()
        self.assertEqual(fills, ["29", "29"])
        self.assertIn("BLOCKED: you sent exactly these actions", asked[3])

    async def test_an_agent_that_can_be_sent_idle_is_left_to_its_own_loop_rules(self):
        async def idle(why):
            return None

        fills, _ = await self.run_agent(idle)
        self.assertEqual(len(fills), 4)
EOF

# QuoteCraft speed plan — tracking table

Goal: **100 quality in under 5:00 (top 10) at lower cost**, keeping the system agentic (the model chooses where to
go, what to search, what matters; code only helps). Work happens on branch `claude/tier1-speed` in the worktree
`D:\Personal_Projects\QuoteCraft-tier1` (package: `starter-kit/`). One change at a time, one test run each; a run
past 5:00 is cancelled and analysed.

Reference: best scored run `run_a176359f` = 100, **6:15, $0.176** (investigation 219 s, bid form + TAN 155 s).
Leaderboard 06:56 UTC: #1 Plite 0:38 $0.026 · #8 Saltovka 5:28 $0.159 · #9 QuoteCraft 6:15 $0.176.

## Runs

| Run | Commit | Quality | Time | Cost | Investigation | Bid form + TAN | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| a176359f (scored) | 2c82a7bf (base) | 100 | 6:15 | $0.176 | 219 s, 155 calls | 155 s, 35 clerk turns | baseline |
| 10def205 (test) | 3fd4d43 | – (looping, cancelled at limit) | >11 min | >$0.37 | 236 s, 364 calls, $0.31 | clerk looped 40+ turns on "Position hinzufügen" | crews + guessed template failed |
| 99f03f3f (test) | e359542 | running | | | | | |

## Changes

Status: ✅ done and verified in a run · 🟨 done, waiting for a run · ❌ tried, made it worse (off) · ⬜ to do

| # | Change | Where | Why (evidence) | Expected gain | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Click on a slow page load counted as done, never pressed twice (`no_wait_after`) | browser_env.py | a176359f: 78 s login click; local run: every cookie/login click "failed" after 6–30 s | up to 1–2 min in bad runs | 🟨 (local ✅) |
| 2 | Playwright timeouts 6 s action / 15 s navigation; step 20 s; fresh tab at first hard failure | browser_env.py, worker.py | a176359f: 125 s lost on one flaky login | up to 2 min in bad runs | 🟨 |
| 3 | `collect`/`fetch` get 75 s | worker.py | local run: a 4-page collect cut at 20 s | correctness | 🟨 |
| 4 | Verification read reused as next page read | worker.py | one page read per turn saved | ~0.3–1 s/turn | 🟨 |
| 5 | History: no earlier page in full (FULL_TURNS=0), 6 turns, older thoughts capped at 16 | worker.py | uncached input = 88% of cost; 10def205: 7.9k vs 10.6k tokens/call | −25–40% cost | ✅ (tokens/call down) |
| 6 | Sites opened + logged in while the brief is read | agent.py | each agent's first turn was the login | ~5–8 s | 🟨 |
| 7 | Hedged model call (2nd request after 12 s or 4× median) | llm.py | past runs: stuck calls cost 120 s each | up to minutes in bad runs | 🟨 |
| 8 | Clerk `enter_positions` template (code repeats the steps for every position) | submit.py | a176359f: 25 of 35 clerk turns = 5 positions one choice per turn | ~80–100 s | 🟨 (first try ❌, see 9) |
| 9 | Clerk enters the FIRST position by hand, template only for the rest; NOT-saved check after the last press | submit.py | 10def205: template guessed "Position hinzufügen" as the save button → loop | makes 8 safe | 🟨 |
| 10 | Clerk loop breaker: same form fills on same page 3× → refused with a way out | worker.py | 10def205: 40+ identical turns until step cap | prevents 0-score runs | 🟨 |
| 11 | TAN request + ask_mail in one reply; TAN + finalize in one reply | submit.py | 2 clerk turns | ~6 s | 🟨 |
| 12 | Crews: 3 ERP + 2 mail agents in parallel tabs | agent.py | idea: ERP 46 serial turns | — | ❌ 10def205: duplicate work, 2× cost, no time gain → default 1 |
| 13 | End the investigation when no question is open and nothing is being read (don't wait for agents re-checking) | agent.py | 10def205: last question closed ~3:34, end 3:56; tender portal browses docs after done | ~20–40 s | ⬜ |
| 14 | Clerk opens the bid form and fills bidder data DURING the investigation | agent.py, submit.py | a176359f: first 4 clerk turns ~15 s after the bid is ready | ~15 s | ⬜ |
| 15 | Stop re-filing loops: an "already filed" keep twice → agent told to finish | agent.py | 10def205: customer portal re-filed requirements 12× | cost | ⬜ |
| 16 | ERP agent must not search before requirements exist (idle instead) | agent.py prompt | 10def205: 16 turns of "Hydraulikzylinder >20 results" | cost | ⬜ |
| 17 | Read-only pages fetched over HTTP with the browser session instead of full render (model still picks the URL) | browser_env.py | each goto+settle 1–3 s | ~20–40 s | ⬜ (risky on unseen sites) |

## Rules for every change

- No value from the public scenario in code, prompts or notes (scan the diff before each run).
- The model decides navigation, searches and relevance; helpers only execute what it chose.
- Run the unit tests (`uv run python -m unittest discover tests`) before a test run; one test run at a time.
- Record every run in the Runs table with its verdict, and every change's status here.

async def end_when_settled(case: CaseFile, team: Team, tasks: list, mail: str | None) -> None:
    """End the investigation as soon as the case file is complete: no open question, nothing still being read, no

    is done) idle. Agents still browsing are stopped. Test run 10def205: the last question closed ~22 s before the

    documents after its questions were answered."""
    since = None
    while not team.finished.is_set():
        await asyncio.sleep(1.0)
        complete = (not case.pending and (mail is None or mail in team.idle or mail not in team.names)
                    and not case.questions())
        if not complete:
            since = None
        elif since is None or since[1] != case.version:
            since = (time.time(), case.version)
        elif time.time() - since[0] >= SETTLED_SECONDS:
            print("Every question is answered and nothing is being read: the investigation ends now", flush=True)
            team.finished.set()
            for task in tasks:
                task.cancel()
            return

content.text:
I checked first: your `starter-kit` is byte-for-byte the package from your best run (`run_a176359f`), and `logs (2).jsonl` is that run's log. The full table is in [BEST_RUN_TIMING.md](BEST_RUN_TIMING.md); times below are on the run page's clock.

## Where the 6:15 goes

| Part | When | Time | Model calls | How the code does it | What happened |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A. Read the brief | 0:00–0:08 | 8 s | 1 | `read_context`: one Qwen call with reasoning on | All agents wait for it |
| B. Investigation (4 sites in parallel) | 0:08–3:41 | **213 s** | 154 | One agent per site: read the page as text → Qwen picks actions → Playwright does them; `keep` → Qwen pulls the facts out of the page | Ends when the slowest agent (tender portal) finishes |
| B1. Tender portal stuck on login | 0:08–2:16 | **128 s wasted** | 2 | The click falls back to waiting Playwright's 30 s default, then a 45 s page-read limit; the tab is replaced only after the 2nd failure | Click hung 78 s, next page read 45 s; the fresh tab then loaded instantly |
| B2. Tender portal real work | 2:16–2:59 | 43 s | 11 | login, cookies, gate, Q&A `collect` (6 pages), positions | Normal, about 4 s per turn |
| B3. Tender portal extra browsing | 2:59–3:40 | **41 s wasted** | 5 | Model re-opens documents it had already filed; a "back" timed out (23 s) | Nothing new found |
| B4. ERP | 0:08–2:48 | 160 s | 45 | Per material: search, open, planning tab, file; then prices ×5; then stock ×5 (3 clicks each) | Next bottleneck once B1 is fixed |
| B5–B6. Mail / supplier portal | done by 1:58 / 1:28 | 110 s / 80 s | 25 / 23 | search, archive, `collect`, file | Fine |
| C. Calculate the bid | 3:41 | <1 s | 0 | `calculator.py` (exact Decimal maths, code only) | — |
| D. Open bid form, company data, bid type | 3:41–4:02 | 21 s | 6 | Clerk agent | Includes 6 s of confusion: the form starts at position 01.04 |
| E. Enter 5 positions | 4:02–5:52 | **110 s** | 23 | Clerk `steps` action, but **one dropdown choice + "Apply" per turn** (5 turns per position) | About 22 s per position |
| F. Discount, declarations, review | 5:52–6:03 | 11 s | 3 | Clerk | Fine |
| G. Get the TAN | 6:03–6:11 | 8 s | 2 | Mailbox helper agent in a new tab | Fine |
| H. Enter TAN, check, submit | 6:11–6:16 | 5 s | 2 | Pre-submit check + final click done in code | Fine |

Every model call waits about 1.1 s in the platform's queue, so each agent turn costs at least 3–4 s with its browser action. The time is set by how many turns run one after another.

## The three things that matter

1. **The login hang on a flaky page: 128 s.** This is a browser timeout problem, not a model problem.
2. **Entering positions one dropdown per turn: about 75 of the 110 s can be cut.**
3. **The tender agent keeps browsing after its job is done: 41 s.**

Fixing those three should bring the run to about **4:00–4:20**, under your 5:00 target, with the same agentic design.

## Where things stand

- My earlier test run with all the changes together **finished at 19.1 quality in 10:28** (only 1 of 5 positions entered, no discount). Going back to your best package was the right call.
- Everything is committed and pushed on `claude/tier1-speed`.
- [SPEED_PLAN.md](SPEED_PLAN.md) records what was tried before.

Section 4 of the timing file lists the order: one fix per test run, starting with the login-hang fix (#1) alone on top of your best package. Shall I make fix #1 and start that test run?

<pasted_content id="614c">
You are Claude working in plan mode on the QuoteCraft RFQ-to-bid agent
for the Atira EHL challenge.

Project context
- The agent runs against 4 websites (tender portal, supplier portal, ERP,
  mail) and currently reaches quality 100 and full eligibility on the
  public dataset.
- The best scored run (run_a176359f, restored in commit 95f075b) has
  time ≈ 00:06:15 and cost ≈ $0.176 on the public leaderboard.
- BEST_RUN_TIMING.md and SPEED_PLAN.md already analyze that run and list
  the main bottlenecks.

Primary objective
- Reduce runtime by at least 60 seconds (target ≈ 4:45–5:15) on the
  public test environment, WITHOUT losing eligibility or reducing
  quality below 100.
- Do this by tightening agent orchestration and browser timings, not by
  changing the RFQ/bid logic or pricing math.

Hard constraints (do NOT violate)
1. Keep the agent fully eligible: every required field must remain
   correct and complete, and the bid must still be submitted.
2. Preserve quality 100: no degradation in field-level correctness or
   evidence handling is acceptable.
3. Do not change:
   - discount and price calculation code,
   - RFQ interpretation logic,
   - bid-to-form reconciliation and pre-submit checks.
4. Keep model cost in the same order of magnitude; do not triple token
   usage just to gain speed.
5. Make changes in small, reviewable steps: one clearly scoped “fix”
   per test run, with comments in SPEED_PLAN.md.

Known time sinks (from BEST_RUN_TIMING.md)
A. Tender portal login hang (~128 s wasted)
   - A click falls back to Playwright’s long default timeout, then a
     long page-read limit; the tab is only replaced after repeated
     failures.
B. Tender portal extra browsing (~41 s wasted)
   - After collecting the needed RFQ facts, the agent keeps reopening
     documents and waiting for “back” operations that don’t add new
     information.
C. Position entry in the bid form (~110 s total)
   - The clerk agent enters positions one dropdown choice per turn,
     with one model call and one browser action per tiny step, leading
     to ≈22 s per position.

Your tasks

Task 1 – Login hang fix (Fix #1)
- Refactor the tender portal agent’s click/wait helper so that:
  - Clicks to login and post-login navigation use a SHORT timeout
    (e.g. 8–10 s) and at most 1–2 retries.
  - Success detection is based on specific DOM markers (e.g. presence
    of the tender dashboard or RFQ list), not on waiting an arbitrary
    30–45 s.
  - Page reads on the tender portal use a tighter cap (e.g. 10–15 s)
    and return as soon as the accessibility tree is stable.
- Ensure failure handling:
  - On a timeout, refresh or reopen the tab once, then retry;
  - If login still fails, log a clear error but do not sit idle for
    another 45 s.
- Update or add tests for the login helper so we can assert:
  - fast success path,
  - controlled failure path with bounded wait,
  - no infinite or 60+ second hangs.

Task 2 – Stop tender agent when its job is done (Fix #2)
- Introduce an explicit “tender_evidence_complete” state:
  - When RFQ specs, positions, Q&A, and any required documents are
    successfully extracted and filed, mark the tender agent as DONE.
- Change the tender agent’s planning logic so that once DONE is reached:
  - It stops proposing navigation actions on the tender portal,
  - It does not reopen already-filed documents,
  - It yields control back to the coordinator.
- Add tests to ensure:
  - After required tender data is present in the shared state, no more
    redundant “open document / back / wait” cycles occur.
  - The agent still extracts all needed tender evidence before stopping.

Task 3 – Batch position entry (Fix #3)
- Redesign the clerk agent’s form-filling strategy so that each turn
  fills an entire position or a large chunk of it, instead of one
  dropdown per turn.
  Concretely:
  - For each position, compose a structured action that sets all fields
    that can be filled from the current bid state in ONE browser step
    (or in at most two steps: one to open the row, one to apply all
    field values).
  - Reduce the number of model turns per position to 1–2, targeting
    ≈5–8 s per position instead of ≈22 s.
- Keep safety:
  - Continue to rely on deterministic code for calculations,
    indices, and value selection.
  - Keep the pre-submit checklist to verify the live form matches the
    intended bid after the batched fill.
- Add tests that:
  - Populate a mock form with multiple positions;
  - Verify that one agent turn correctly fills all fields for a
    position;
  - Confirm that the reconciliation gate still catches mismatches.

Task 4 – Measurement and documentation
- After each fix is implemented:
  - Run a sandbox test on the same environment as run_a176359f.
  - Record time and cost in BEST_RUN_TIMING.md and SPEED_PLAN.md.
  - Explain briefly which fix was applied and how it changed timing
    (e.g. “login hang reduced from 128 s wasted to <20 s total”).
- Only stack fixes together after each one has been validated alone:
  - First run: Fix #1 only, on top of the restored best package.
  - Second run: Fix #1 + Fix #2.
  - Third run: Fix #1 + Fix #2 + Fix #3.
  - Stop stacking if any fix causes a regression in eligibility or
    quality.

Workstyle requirements
- Use plan mode: first list the files you will edit and the diffs you
  propose, then apply them.
- Preserve the structure of the existing multi-agent design; do not
  introduce new agents or major refactors.
- Keep code changes tight and well-commented around the timing-critical
  paths (login helper, tender agent planner, clerk form-filling).
- When you are done, summarize:
  - The new measured runtime and cost,
  - Which bottlenecks were removed,
  - Which risks were introduced and how they are mitigated.

Goal check
- The work is successful only if:
  - The agent still produces an eligible, quality-100 bid, and
  - Runtime is reduced by at least 60 seconds compared to 6:15, with
    no major cost blow-up.

    async def run(self) -> dict:
        results: list[str] = []

        self.log(f"starting at {self.tab.base_url}")
        if self.tab.page.url in ("", "about:blank"):
            try:

            except asyncio.TimeoutError:
                results.append(f"opening {self.tab.base_url} took longer than {STEP_TIMEOUT} s; reload or try again")
        repeats, last_signature, failures = 0, "", 0
        seen_signatures: dict[str, int] = {}
        stuck = 0  # page reads and navigations in a row that timed out or failed: the tab may be broken
        while self.steps < self.max_steps and time.time() < self.deadline:
            self.steps += 1

class Team:
    """Holds an agent that has nothing to do until the case file brings news, and ends the investigation when every
    agent is idle and no filed document is still being read."""

    def __init__(self, case: CaseFile, names: list[str], deadline: float):
        self.case, self.names, self.deadline = case, set(names), deadline
        self.idle: set[str] = set()
        self.finished = asyncio.Event()
        self.woken: dict[str, float] = {}  # when an agent was last woken for finished reading (at most every 30 s)

    def release(self, name: str, candidates: set[str]) -> None:
        """A routed agent (ERP or mail) went idle leaving `candidates` open and nothing is being read any more: those
        go to every agent (RELEASED), and the others are woken by a case-file change. Questions that turn up while it
        is idle are its own work (it is woken for them), so only the ones open when it went idle are candidates."""
        if self.case.pending or site_role(name) is None:
            return
        still = {qid for qid, _ in self.case.questions()} & candidates
        fresh = still - RELEASED
        if fresh:
            RELEASED.update(fresh)
            print(f"[{name}] left open, now offered to every agent: {', '.join(sorted(fresh))}", flush=True)
            bump = getattr(self.case, "_bump", None)
            if bump:
                bump()

    def hook(self, name: str):
        async def hold(why: str) -> str | None:
            before = {qid for qid, _ in questions_for_site(name, self.case.questions())}
            self.release(name, before)
            version = self.case.version
            # Documents still being read when the agent went idle: once one of them is done, the agent is woken if
            # questions are still open. Sandbox run 024bd2ac: the ERP agent went idle "until the requirements are
            # read" with its material questions already open; they were never new, so it slept for 400 s.
            reading = self.case.pending
            self.idle.add(name)
            try:
                while not self.finished.is_set() and time.time() < self.deadline:
                    changed = await self.case.wait_change(version, 1.0)
                    if self.finished.is_set():
                        break
                    if changed:
                        self.release(name, before)
                        version = self.case.version
                        fresh = {qid for qid, _ in questions_for_site(name, self.case.questions())} - before
                        if fresh or self.case.news.get(name):
                            return "The case file has news" + (f"; new open questions: {', '.join(sorted(fresh))}" if fresh else "") + "."
                        still_open = {qid for qid, _ in questions_for_site(name, self.case.questions())}
                        rested = time.time() - self.woken.get(name, 0.0) >= 30
                        if reading and self.case.pending < reading and still_open and rested:
                            self.woken[name] = time.time()
                            return ("Documents that were still being read are now in the case file. Open questions: "
                                    f"{', '.join(sorted(still_open))}. Work on those your website can answer.")
                    elif self.idle == self.names and self.case.pending == 0:
                        self.finished.set()
                return None
            finally:
                self.idle.discard(name)
        return hold

import unittest

    line = Line("1", "M-1", 40, unit_price=Decimal("12.50"), lead_time_weeks=3)
    return Bid("T-0001", "bid", Decimal("2.5"), [line], Decimal("500.00"))


class ReviewPages(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_renamed_and_reordered_review_fields_still_pass(self):
        page = "Bestellübersicht\nEUR 500,00\nArtikel 1 / M-1\nVorgang T-0001\n[8] button \"Endgültig bestätigen\""
        report = check(page, bid(), "T-0001")
        self.assertTrue(report.ready, report.text())

    def test_visible_validation_error_and_required_input_block_finalisation(self):
        page = ('T-0001\nPosition 1\nTotal 500.00\n'
                '[3] input "VAT ID" value="" (required)\n(error) Please complete highlighted fields')
        report = check(page, bid(), "T-0001")
        self.assertFalse(report.ready)
        self.assertEqual(len(report.blockers), 2)

    def test_a_page_that_does_not_show_the_bid_is_not_ready_but_reports_no_error(self):
        report = check('[9] button "Continue"', bid(), "T-0001")
        self.assertFalse(report.ready)

        self.assertIn("total 500.00", " ".join(report.unproven))
        self.assertIn("NOT SHOWN", report.text())
        self.assertIn("review or summary step", report.text())

        no_bid = Bid("T-0001", "no_bid", Decimal("0"), [], Decimal("0"))

"""The speed fixes of BEST_RUN_TIMING.md, measured on run a176359f (100, 6:15):

Fix #1  a page that cannot be read is a broken tab: replaced at once, within a bounded wait (128 s were lost on one
        flaky tender-portal login).
Fix #2  the tender agent stops once its evidence is on file: the Q&A list followed to its end closes its question by
        itself (41 s of re-opened documents), and routine "document read" notices no longer wake an idle agent.
(Fix #3, the clerk's enter_positions, is tested in test_enter_positions.py; the browser side of Fix #1 in
test_browser_env.py.)"""
import asyncio
import sys
import time
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import patch

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

import agent  # noqa: E402
import llm  # noqa: E402
import worker  # noqa: E402
from casefile import CaseFile  # noqa: E402
from worker import Agent  # noqa: E402

CONTEXT = {"tender_reference": "T-0001", "scenario_date": "2030-03-01T09:00:00+00:00"}


class HangingTab:
    """Its first page read never finishes; after `renew` every read answers at once."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.site_id, self.base_url = "portal", "http://portal.test"
        self.page = SimpleNamespace(url=self.base_url + "/login", main_frame=SimpleNamespace(evaluate=self._alive))
        self.document, self.document_source = "", ""
        self.renewals, self.reads = 0, 0

    async def _alive(self, script):
        return True

    def take_events(self):
        return []

    async def observe(self):
        self.reads += 1
        if self.renewals == 0:
            await asyncio.sleep(30)
        return 'url: http://portal.test/home\ntitle: Home\n[1] button "Go"'

    async def renew(self):
        self.renewals += 1
        return "opened http://portal.test/"


class Fix1BrokenTabIsReplacedAtOnce(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    async def test_a_page_read_that_hangs_gets_a_fresh_tab_within_a_bounded_wait(self):
        tab, asked = HangingTab(), []

        async def model(messages, **kwargs):
            asked.append(messages[-1]["content"])
            return {"thought": "", "actions": [{"do": "done", "summary": "ok"}]}

        started = time.monotonic()
        with patch.object(llm, "chat_json", model), patch.object(worker, "READ_TIMEOUT", 0.3):
            outcome = await Agent("portal", tab, "system", lambda: "job", max_steps=3).run()
        self.assertTrue(outcome["done"])
        self.assertEqual(tab.renewals, 1)
        self.assertLess(time.monotonic() - started, 5)  # not 45 s of waiting, then a second failure
        self.assertIn("replaced by a fresh one", asked[0])
        self.assertIn("title: Home", asked[0])  # the model sees the fresh tab's page, not a timeout message


class Fix2QuestionCloses(unittest.TestCase):
    def case(self) -> CaseFile:
        case = CaseFile("BRIEF", CONTEXT)
        case.merge("clarifications", {"answers": [{"number": "Q-1", "timestamp": "2030-02-01T10:00:00Z"}]})
        return case

    def test_the_q_and_a_followed_to_its_end_and_read_closes_its_question(self):
        case = self.case()
        self.assertIn("clarifications", [qid for qid, _ in case.questions()])  # filed, but nobody vouched for "all"
        case.listed_in_full["clarifications"] = "portal"
        self.assertNotIn("clarifications", [qid for qid, _ in case.questions()])
        self.assertEqual(case.answers["clarifications"][0], "complete")

    def test_it_stays_open_while_the_list_is_still_being_read(self):
        case = self.case()
        case.listed_in_full["clarifications"] = "portal"
        case.pending_by_agent["portal"] = 1
        self.assertIn("clarifications", [qid for qid, _ in case.questions()])


class PortalTab:
    def __init__(self):
        self.site_id, self.base_url = "portal", "http://portal.test"
        self.page = SimpleNamespace(url=self.base_url + "/qa")
        self.document, self.document_source = "", ""
        self.last_collect = None


class Fix2KeepMarksAWholeList(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    async def keep(self, held_by: str, run: dict | None) -> CaseFile:
        case = CaseFile("BRIEF", CONTEXT)
        team = agent.Team(case, ["portal"], time.time() + 600)
        tab = PortalTab()
        tab.last_collect = run
        investigator = agent.investigator(case, team, tab, time.time() + 600)
        investigator.held = ("Q-1 answered: quantity of position 1 is 40. " * 3, "http://portal.test/qa")
        investigator.held_by = held_by

        async def nothing(*args, **kwargs):
            return {}

        with patch.object(llm, "chat_json", nothing):
            said = await investigator.extra["keep"]({"do": "keep", "kind": "clarifications"})
            await asyncio.sleep(0.05)  # let the background extraction finish
        self.assertTrue(said.startswith("filed"), said)
        return case

    async def test_a_list_collected_to_its_end_is_marked(self):
        case = await self.keep("collect", {"pages": 6, "capped": False})
        self.assertEqual(case.listed_in_full, {"clarifications": "portal"})

    async def test_a_capped_list_a_single_page_or_a_download_is_not(self):
        for held_by, run in (("collect", {"pages": 10, "capped": True}), ("collect", {"pages": 1, "capped": False}),
                             ("fetch", {"pages": 6, "capped": False})):
            case = await self.keep(held_by, run)
            self.assertEqual(case.listed_in_full, {}, (held_by, run))


class Fix2RoutineNewsDoesNotWake(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    async def hold_with(self, news: str):
        agent.SITE_ROLES.clear()
        case = CaseFile("BRIEF", CONTEXT)
        team = agent.Team(case, ["portal"], time.time() + 600)
        waiting = asyncio.ensure_future(team.hook("portal")("done"))
        await asyncio.sleep(0.2)
        case.news.setdefault("portal", []).append(news)
        case._bump()
        return await asyncio.wait_for(waiting, 10), team

    async def test_a_document_that_was_read_fine_lets_the_agent_rest(self):
        woke, team = await self.hold_with("From the positions document you filed (http://x): 1: 40 pcs -> A-1")
        self.assertIsNone(woke)  # not woken; the investigation ends with every agent idle
        self.assertTrue(team.finished.is_set())

    async def test_a_document_that_failed_wakes_the_agent(self):
        woke, _ = await self.hold_with("From the positions document you filed (http://x): the extraction failed; "
                                       "file the document again")
        self.assertIn("The case file has news", woke)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()


It is your best package (`run_a176359f`) plus the three fixes; nothing else was changed. As you asked, I didn't run anything locally. The tests for each fix are written but not run; I only checked that the code parses. A dry-run pack lists 70 files: your package plus 3 new test files, no logs, no virtualenv.

| Fix | Problem in your best run | What changed | Expected saving |
|---|---|---|---|
| **#1 Login hang** | 128 s lost on one tender-portal login | A click that starts a slow page load counts as done and is never pressed twice. Element waits are 8 s and page loads 15 s (were 30–45 s). Login success means the password field is gone; if the login form is still there, that's reported after at most 8 s. If a page can't be read within 15 s, or the tab breaks, it gets a fresh tab immediately. Paging through lists and file downloads keep 75 s. | up to ~2 min whenever a page is flaky |
| **#2 Tender agent stops** | 41 s re-opening documents after its job was done | The Q&A question closes by itself once the agent has paged through the Q&A list to its end and filed it. A routine "your document was read" notice no longer wakes an idle agent; only new questions or problem notices do. | 20–40 s, plus fewer wasted model calls |
| **#3 Positions in bulk** | 110 s, one dropdown per turn | The clerk enters the first position itself and sees which button saves it. Then one action repeats exactly those steps for every other position, in whatever order the form shows them. A position still on screen after the last press is reported as **not saved** rather than counted. | 60–75 s |

Expected total with all three: **about 4:00–4:45**, against 6:15.

**What I deliberately left out**, because it broke my earlier test runs:
- shorter agent memory (the ERP agent looped 121 turns);
- parallel ERP/mail agents (doubled the cost);
- the repeated-action blocker (it stopped the mailbox helper from re-unlocking the inbox, so no TAN);
- ending the investigation early;
- changes to the signing and review steps.

The price calculation, how the tender is read, and the pre-submit checks are untouched.

**Risks to watch:**
- **The Q&A auto-close (#2)** only fires when the Q&A list was paged to its end over at least 2 pages. If the private sites keep amendments outside that list, the tender agent could stop before filing them. If you see that, this is the one to switch off.
- **Positions (#3):** look for `[submit] enter_positions: position … entered` four times after the clerk's first position. A "was NOT saved" message means the clerk picked the wrong save button. The safeguard stops it there, and the clerk then continues step by step from that position.

**One thing I fixed in the folder:** a log from your run `run_fa240524` had been copied into `starter-kit`, and it would have been uploaded with the agent, including the run's values and TAN. I moved it to `QuoteCraft-tier1\logs-moved-out-of-starter-kit.jsonl`. Please keep logs outside `starter-kit`.

content.text:
Yes, but only for the mechanical steps. If code starts taking the decisions (where to click, what to search, which record counts), the reviewer rejects the package as "a script instead of an agent". It would also break on the private sites, which use different software and layouts. Your run shows which steps are mechanical and worth converting.

**What happened in your run (`run_20e3c020`): 100 quality, 7:38, $0.248**

| Part | Your run | Best run | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reading the brief | 11 s | 8 s | One model call with reasoning on |
| Investigation | **315 s** | 213 s | The ERP agent needed **92 model calls** (46 in the best run). Two first clicks (tender, mail) also hung for 35 s each before the tab was replaced. |
| Bid form + TAN | 142 s | 155 s | The clerk now does a whole position in one turn, but each such turn takes **11 s of browser time**, because the code re-reads the whole page before every one of its 17 small steps |

The model wasn't slow here. The ERP agent took too many steps, and our own code was slow inside each step.

**What I'd move into code (allowed, and works on unseen sites)**

| # | Make it code | Saves | Allowed? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **ERP batching:** after the model has opened one material and seen which tabs hold the facts, code opens the other materials and files the same tabs. The `file_each` action already does this, but the ERP agent never uses it. I'd make it the expected way of working whenever several materials are open. | **60–120 s** and about half the ERP cost | Yes: the model still picks the materials and tabs; code only clicks |
| 2 | **Faster form steps:** find each field by its label directly, instead of re-reading the whole page 17 times per position | about 30 s | Yes: pure speed-up, no decisions |
| 3 | **Login and cookie banner by code** on all 4 sites at once, while the brief is being read | about 8 s and 8 model calls | Yes: filling the login form and choosing "necessary cookies only" |
| 4 | **Read the brief without reasoning** (with reasoning only if the reference or date is missing) | 5–9 s | Yes |

**What I would not do:** hard-code paths like "ERP → MM03 → planning tab", fixed button names, or the order of the bid form. That's exactly what the reviewer rejects, and it would fail on the private sites.

Together, 1–4 should take your run from 7:38 to roughly **4:30–5:00**, and the cost down about 30%. One caveat: the same package varies by ±1 minute between runs (6:15 vs 7:38) because teammates' test runs share the model queue. Run the final candidate twice before judging it.

Shall I implement 1–4 now, in the same folder, on top of the current files?

async def solve(task: dict, playwright) -> dict | None:
    started = time.time()
    sites = [site for site in task.get("access") or [] if isinstance(site, dict) and site.get("siteId") and site.get("url")]
    only = {name for name in os.environ.get("AGENT_SITES", "").split(",") if name}
    if not sites or not task.get("brief"):
        return None
    brief = task["brief"]
    listing = "\n".join(f"- {site['siteId']}: {site['url']}" for site in sites)
    context = await read_context(brief + f"\n\nThe websites of this run:\n{listing}")
    SITE_ROLES.clear()
    RELEASED.clear()
    SITE_ROLES.update({role: str(context.get(f"{role}_site") or "") for role in ("erp", "mail")
                       if str(context.get(f"{role}_site") or "") in {site["siteId"] for site in sites}})
    case = CaseFile(brief, context)
    print(f"Sanity checks on: {', '.join(sanity.active()) or 'none'}", flush=True)
    print(f"Context: tender {case.reference}, scenario {case.scenario.isoformat()}, company {case.company}, "
          f"senders {case.senders}", flush=True)

    left = contract.seconds_left(task)
    budget = min(left, 20 * 60) if left != float("inf") else 20 * 60  # a scored run has 20 minutes
    hard_stop = started + budget - 45
    # The bid form takes ~2 min and the signing code another 1-2 min; a signed partial bid scores, an unsigned
    # complete one does not. So the investigation ends with 8 minutes left (sandbox test run 54c78c38: 330 s was
    # too little and the run ended unsigned).
    submit_reserve = min(480, budget * 0.4)
    investigate_until = hard_stop - submit_reserve

    opened, tabs = await open_tabs(playwright, sites)
    try:
        working = [tab for name, tab in tabs.items() if not only or name in only]
        team = Team(case, [tab.site_id for tab in working], investigate_until)
        async def bounded(tab):  # an agent stuck past the deadline is stopped so that the others' facts still count
            restarted = False
            while True:
                limit = max(10.0, investigate_until - time.time() + 20)
                try:
                    outcome = await asyncio.wait_for(investigator(case, team, tab, investigate_until).run(), limit)
                except asyncio.TimeoutError:
                    team.finished.set()
                    return RuntimeError(f"stopped after {limit:.0f} s: still busy at the investigation deadline")
                # Weak sandbox runs (10, 22.8, 27.8, 29.1) had agents end with done: false while time was left. One
                # fresh start, with a clean conversation in a new tab, instead of giving the site up (sanity.py).
                if (sanity.enabled("agent_restart") and not restarted and not outcome.get("done")
                        and investigate_until - time.time() > RESTART_MIN_SECONDS and case.questions()):
                    restarted = True
                    print(f"[{tab.site_id}] stopped unfinished after {outcome.get('steps')} steps; restarting once "
                          "in a fresh tab", flush=True)
                    try:
                        await asyncio.wait_for(tab.renew(), 45)
                    except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001
                        print(f"[{tab.site_id}] could not renew the tab: {str(error)[:150]}", flush=True)
                    continue
                return outcome
        outcomes = await asyncio.gather(*(bounded(tab) for tab in working), return_exceptions=True)
        for tab, outcome in zip(working, outcomes):
            print(f"[{tab.site_id}] finished: {outcome if isinstance(outcome, Exception) else json.dumps(outcome, ensure_ascii=False)[:300]}", flush=True)
        for _ in range(40):  # facts of the last filed documents
            if not case.pending:

FILE_EACH_LIMIT = 12  # records per file_each action
FILE_EACH_SECONDS = 150  # and seconds for all of them; the agent continues from the list afterwards
# #1: the ERP agent worked every record by hand, one click per model turn: 46 turns in run a176359f, 92 in 20e3c020
# (search, open, a tab, file; then each price view; then each stock breakdown). file_each lets code open and file
# the records the model names, with the tabs and paths it learned on the first one; it was never used.
RECORD_BATCH = ("SAVE TURNS: {count} record questions are open on your website. Work ONE candidate record by hand "
                "and see which of its tabs, and which chain of controls (for example down into a stock breakdown, or "
                "into a price-scale view), hold the facts the questions ask for. Then file the other candidates of a "
                "result list with ONE file_each: their links, plus those tabs and paths, each with its kind. Code "
                "opens and files every record and comes back to the list; do not open them one by one.")
BATCH_NUDGE_AFTER = 3  # same-kind pages filed one by one before file_each is suggested once


def batch_hint(counter: dict, kind: str, filed: bool) -> str:
    """Suggest file_each once an agent has filed the same kind of page one by one BATCH_NUDGE_AFTER times. `counter`
    maps kind -> consecutive filings (mutated). Fires once per streak; the model still decides."""
    if not filed or not kind:
        return ""
    counter[kind] = counter.get(kind, 0) + 1
    for other in [key for key in counter if key != kind]:
        counter.pop(other, None)
    if counter[kind] == BATCH_NUDGE_AFTER:
        return ("; you have now filed several pages of this kind one by one: if the list they came from still shows "
                "more records of the same kind, go back to that list and file the rest together with one file_each "
                "(naming the records and the tabs or paths that hold the facts)")
    return ""

class FastSteps(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    """#2: a steps chain reuses its last page read while it only fills fields; a press reads the page again."""

    async def test_fills_reuse_the_read_and_a_press_reads_again(self):
        class Form:
            def __init__(self):
                self.base_url = "http://form.test"
                self.page = SimpleNamespace(url=self.base_url + "/f", main_frame=SimpleNamespace(evaluate=self._alive))
                self.document, self.document_source, self.reads, self.values = "", "", 0, {}

            async def _alive(self, script):
                return True

            def take_events(self):
                return []

            async def observe(self):
                self.reads += 1
                return ('url: http://form.test/f\\n[1] input "Quantity" value=""\\n[2] input "Price" value=""\\n'
                        '[3] input "Weeks" value=""\\n[4] button "Save"')

            async def fill(self, aid, text, enter=False):
                self.values[aid] = text
                return f"filled [{aid}]"

            async def click(self, aid):
                self.values["saved"] = True
                return f"clicked [{aid}]"

        form = Form()
        steps = [{"field": "Quantity", "value": "40"}, {"field": "Price", "value": "12,50"},
                 {"field": "Weeks", "value": "3"}, {"press": "Save"}]
        said = await Agent("submit", form, "system", lambda: "job")._steps(steps)
        self.assertTrue(said.startswith("ran all 4 steps"), said)
        self.assertEqual(form.values, {"1": "40", "2": "12,50", "3": "3", "saved": True})
        self.assertEqual(form.reads, 2)  # one read for the three fills, one after the press (was 5)

    async def test_a_control_gone_since_the_read_is_found_again(self):
        class Rerendering:
            base_url = "http://form.test"

            def __init__(self):
                self.page = SimpleNamespace(url=self.base_url + "/f", main_frame=SimpleNamespace(evaluate=self._alive))
                self.document, self.document_source, self.offset, self.values = "", "", 0, {}

            async def _alive(self, script):
                return True

            def take_events(self):
                return []

            async def observe(self):
                return f'url: http://form.test/f\\n[{1 + self.offset}] input "A" value=""\\n[{2 + self.offset}] input "B" value=""'

            async def fill(self, aid, text, enter=False):
                if int(aid) < 1 + self.offset:
                    return f"there is no element [{aid}] on the page any more"
                self.values[text] = aid
                self.offset += 10  # every fill re-renders the form with new ids
                return f"filled [{aid}]"

        form = Rerendering()
        said = await Agent("submit", form, "system", lambda: "job")._steps(
            [{"field": "A", "value": "a"}, {"field": "B", "value": "b"}])
        self.assertTrue(said.startswith("ran all 2 steps"), said)
        self.assertEqual(set(form.values), {"a", "b"})

            return {"thought": "", "actions": [{"do": "done", "summary": "ok"}]}

3. Those extra turns also crowd the shared model queue.

I'll check how the routing tests describe what other agents should see, then fix all three.

"""Specialized investigators wake only for questions their portal can answer."""
import asyncio
import sys
import time
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

import agent  # noqa: E402
from agent import Team, batch_hint, questions_for_site  # noqa: E402


class FakeCase:
    def __init__(self):
        self.version = 0
        self.pending = 0
        self.news = {}
        self.open_questions = [("mailbox", "Find the sales mailbox.")]
        self.changed = asyncio.Event()

    def questions(self):
        return list(self.open_questions)

    async def wait_change(self, seen, timeout):
        """As CaseFile.wait_change: clear first, then wait, so an old signal does not count as a new change."""
        if self.version == seen:
            self.changed.clear()
            try:
                await asyncio.wait_for(self.changed.wait(), timeout)
            except asyncio.TimeoutError:
                return False
        return self.version != seen

    def update(self, question):
        self.open_questions.append(question)
        self.version += 1
        self.changed.set()


class QuestionRouting(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        agent.SITE_ROLES.clear()
        agent.RELEASED.clear()

    tearDown = setUp

    def test_erp_and_mail_receive_only_resolvable_questions(self):
        questions = [
            ("positions", "Find tender positions."),
            ("material:REQ-1", "Find a matching ERP material."),
            ("data:MAT-1", "Find missing ERP data."),
            ("discount", "Find discount approval."),
            ("reserve:REQ-2", "Find technical release."),
        ]

        self.assertEqual([qid for qid, _ in questions_for_site("erp", questions)],
                         ["material:REQ-1", "data:MAT-1"])
        self.assertEqual([qid for qid, _ in questions_for_site("mail", questions)],
                         ["discount", "reserve:REQ-2"])
        self.assertEqual(questions_for_site("new-portal", questions), questions)

    def test_routing_follows_the_roles_read_from_the_brief_not_the_site_names(self):
        """The private dataset uses other site names (brief: other software, layout and site names)."""
        questions = [("positions", "p"), ("material:REQ-1", "m"), ("discount", "d"), ("reserve:REQ-2", "r")]
        try:
            agent.SITE_ROLES.update({"erp": "warenwirtschaft", "mail": "postfach"})
            self.assertEqual([q for q, _ in questions_for_site("warenwirtschaft", questions)], ["material:REQ-1"])
            self.assertEqual([q for q, _ in questions_for_site("postfach", questions)], ["discount", "reserve:REQ-2"])
            # a site that merely contains "mail" in its name but is not the mailbox gets everything
            self.assertEqual(questions_for_site("mailing-list-portal", questions), questions)
        finally:
            agent.SITE_ROLES.clear()


    async def test_a_routed_question_left_open_is_offered_to_every_agent(self):
        """The private dataset may split facts differently: here the packaging tariff sits in the ERP, so the mail
        agent finishes without it. The question must reach the ERP agent instead of staying with nobody."""
        case = FakeCase()
        case.open_questions = [("packaging_tariff:PKG-9", "the tariff"), ("material:REQ-1", "the material")]
        case._bump = lambda: (setattr(case, "version", case.version + 1), case.changed.set())
        team = Team(case, ["erp", "mail"], time.time() + 5)
        try:
            agent.SITE_ROLES.update({"erp": "erp", "mail": "mail"})
            erp_waiting = asyncio.create_task(team.hook("erp")("done"))  # ERP finished its own question set
            await asyncio.sleep(0.02)
            self.assertIn("material:REQ-1", agent.RELEASED)  # ERP went idle with it open and nothing being read
            mail_waiting = asyncio.create_task(team.hook("mail")("done"))  # mail finished without the tariff
            news = await asyncio.wait_for(erp_waiting, 2)
            self.assertIn("packaging_tariff:PKG-9", news or "")
            self.assertIn("packaging_tariff:PKG-9", [q for q, _ in questions_for_site("erp", case.questions())])
            mail_waiting.cancel()
        finally:
            agent.SITE_ROLES.clear()
            agent.RELEASED.clear()

    def test_nothing_is_released_while_documents_are_still_being_read(self):
        case = FakeCase()
        case.open_questions = [("packaging_tariff:PKG-9", "the tariff")]
        case.pending = 1
        Team(case, ["mail"], time.time() + 5).release("mail", {"packaging_tariff:PKG-9"})
        self.assertEqual(agent.RELEASED, set())

    async def test_erp_idle_hook_ignores_new_mail_questions(self):
        case = FakeCase()
        team = Team(case, ["erp"], time.time() + 5)
        hook = team.hook("erp")
        waiting = asyncio.create_task(hook("done"))
        await asyncio.sleep(0)

        case.update(("discount", "Find discount approval."))
        await asyncio.sleep(0.02)
        self.assertFalse(waiting.done())

        case.update(("material:REQ-1", "Find a matching ERP material."))
        self.assertIn("material:REQ-1", await waiting)


class BatchHint(unittest.TestCase):
    """The file_each nudge: suggest batching once after repeated one-by-one filings of one kind."""

    def test_fires_once_after_three_same_kind_filings(self):
        counter: dict = {}
        self.assertEqual(batch_hint(counter, "material", True), "")
        self.assertEqual(batch_hint(counter, "material", True), "")
        hint = batch_hint(counter, "material", True)
        self.assertIn("file_each", hint)
        self.assertEqual(batch_hint(counter, "material", True), "")  # only once per streak

    def test_a_different_kind_resets_the_streak(self):
        counter: dict = {}
        batch_hint(counter, "material", True)
        batch_hint(counter, "material", True)
        self.assertEqual(batch_hint(counter, "price_conditions", True), "")
        self.assertEqual(batch_hint(counter, "material", True), "")
        self.assertEqual(batch_hint(counter, "material", True), "")
        self.assertIn("file_each", batch_hint(counter, "material", True))

    def test_nothing_filed_or_no_kind_is_silent(self):
        counter: dict = {}
        self.assertEqual(batch_hint(counter, "material", False), "")
        self.assertEqual(batch_hint(counter, "", True), "")
        self.assertEqual(counter, {})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

async def file_each_action(action: dict) -> str:
        said = await file_each(tab, action, lambda kind, text, source: case.file(kind, text, source, name),
                               agent.coverage.saw, deadline, agent.page_seen)
        # The pages it filed are read in a few seconds. Round-3 run: the ERP agent took a status still being read
        # for "did not parse" and opened the same pages again (3 extra turns); its next turn now sees the facts.
        until = min(deadline, time.time() + FILED_READ_WAIT)
        while case.pending_for(name) and time.time() < until:
            await case.wait_change(case.version, min(1.0, max(0.0, until - time.time())))
        return said + ("\nThe filed pages have been read: their facts are in the case file above."
                       if not case.pending_for(name) else
                       "\nSome filed pages are still being read; their facts follow as news. Do not open them again.")

content.text:
Round 4 is committed and pushed (5aadc6d), in the same folder, `D:\Personal_Projects\QuoteCraft-tier1\starter-kit`. As before I only checked that the files parse; nothing was run, and the scan for public-scenario values is clean.

```bash
atira test-run D:/Personal_Projects/QuoteCraft-tier1/starter-kit --challenge rfq
```

**What I changed, from your log:**

| # | What the log showed | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| A | The ERP agent used `file_each` only for the two plain tabs, then clicked into stock (3 clicks) and prices (2 clicks) by hand for every material, about 6 turns each. | The hint now asks it to repeat **every** click from the first material in one `file_each`, with the stock and price chains written as paths, and shows the exact format to use. |
| B | The supplier-portal agent searched its own documents for about 25 turns for a record that lives in the mailbox. The tender agent was woken 6 times by new ERP questions just to say "done". | Agents other than ERP and mail no longer see the ERP's and mailbox's questions. They only get one if the ERP or mail agent gives up on it and it is handed to everyone. |
| C | The ERP agent re-opened pages it had just filed ("status didn't parse") because their facts were still being read. | After a `file_each`, the agent waits up to 10 s for those pages to be read before its next turn. |

**What "verification: steps visibly changed the page state" means:** after every browser action, our code reads the page again and compares it with the page before the action. It then tells the model either "visibly changed the page state" or "caused no visible page change". The comparison ignores the numbered ids, which change on every read.

- **Why it's there:** these portals often swallow a click or silently refuse a value. Without this line, the model would assume every action worked and keep going on a page that never changed. It's also how loops like "clicking a disabled link" get noticed.
- **What it costs:** one page re-read, about 0.3 s per action, and no model call. "Visibly changed" is the normal, good outcome. Only "caused no visible page change" points to a problem.
- **It isn't where the time goes.** In your log, nearly every slow part is a model turn: 2–3 s each, plus about 1 s waiting in the platform's queue. That's why these fixes target the number of turns.

When you run this version, check that the ERP's `file_each` lines include `"path": [...]` entries, and that the supplier-portal agent finishes soon after filing its requirements. Section 6 of `BEST_RUN_TIMING.md` has an empty row for the result.

content.text:
Cost depends only on **tokens sent to and from the model**. The number of calls doesn't matter by itself, and browser time is free.

For Qwen, per million tokens:
- **Input: $0.15**
- **Cached input** (a prompt start the model has seen before): **$0.016**
- **Output: $0.47**

Your $0.223 run:
- 1.32M new input tokens × $0.15/M = **$0.198** (about 89% of the cost)
- 0.68M cached tokens × $0.016/M = $0.011
- 30k output tokens × $0.47/M = $0.014

So **input tokens are almost the whole bill**. Every call re-sends about 9k tokens (instructions, case file, history and the current page). Fewer calls and shorter prompts are therefore what cut the cost. The ranking then multiplies cost × time.

# Run ab00e578: three of four ERP file_each actions filed no stock or price page, so the model clicked them all again
# by hand (~8 turns per material, ERP 53 turns, investigation 302 s). Two causes, both handled in code here:
# 1. a label shown twice on a record page (once in the menu, once for the record): pick_control takes the one whose
#    address belongs to the record, or either one when both lead to the same address;
# 2. a notice page or dialog put in front of the record ("maintenance note ... accept and continue"): pass_notice
#    presses its single way forward, as the model does in its own turns, but only on a page without input fields.
NOTICE_PAGE = re.compile(r"hinweis|wartung|maintenance|notice|meldung|achtung|attention|information|bestätig|confirm",
                         re.I)
NOTICE_GO = re.compile(r"akzeptier|fortfahren|weiter|continue|accept|proceed|verstanden|got it|schließen|close|"
                       r"\bok\b|bestätigen|confirm", re.I)


def pick_control(page: str, label: str, kinds: tuple[str, ...], url: str) -> tuple[str | None, str]:
    """find_control, and when the label is ambiguous: the controls if they all lead to the same address, else the
    one control whose address carries a value of the current page's address (the record's own link)."""
    aid, why = find_control(page, label, kinds)
    if aid is not None or "controls are labelled" not in why:
        return aid, why
    ids = re.findall(r"\[(\d+)\]", why.split(":", 1)[0] if "):" in why else why)
    targets = {m.group(1): (re.search(r"->\s*(\S+)", m.group(4)) or [None, None])[1]
               for m in CONTROL.finditer(page) if m.group(1) in ids}
    addresses = set(targets.values())
    if len(addresses) == 1 and None not in addresses:
        return ids[0], why
    query = urlparse(url)
    tokens = [value for values in parse_qs(query.query).values() for value in values if len(value) >= 3]
    tokens += [part for part in query.path.split("/") if len(part) >= 4]
    scoped = [aid for aid, target in targets.items() if target and any(token in target for token in tokens)]
    if len(scoped) == 1:
        return scoped[0], why
    return None, why


async def pass_notice(tab, page: str) -> str | None:
    """A notice in front of the page (a dialog, or a short page that announces something) with a single way forward
    and no input field: press it and say what was pressed; None leaves the page as it is."""
    modal = "!! A MODAL DIALOG" in page
    area = page.split("!! END OF MODAL DIALOG")[0] if modal else page
    if not modal and (len(page) > 2500 or not NOTICE_PAGE.search(page)):
        return None
    controls = [(m.group(1), m.group(2), m.group(3)) for m in CONTROL.finditer(area)]
    if any(kind.split("(")[0] in ("input", "select", "checkbox", "radio", "switch") for _, kind, _ in controls):
        return None  # a check to pass or a form to fill is the model's
    forward = list(dict.fromkeys(aid for aid, kind, label in controls
                                 if kind in ("button", "link", "clickable") and NOTICE_GO.search(label)))
    if len(forward) != 1:
        return None
    label = next(label for aid, _, label in controls if aid == forward[0])
    await tab.click(forward[0])
    return label
