tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall
tools.description:
Render an inline card of plugins the user can add to claude.ai, taken from SearchPlugins results. The card handles all install UI; do not describe the plugins in text.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. Also when they ask for plugin recommendations. First call SearchPlugins with keywords drawn from the task, then pass the relevant results here: pluginId from each result's id, pluginName from its name, description as returned. Set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). Use ListPlugins for plugins they already have.

After the card, continue the task. Example: "ship this to staging" and a deploy plugin that is not enabled → contextLabel "For your deploys".

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a plugin would help, when SearchPlugins returned nothing relevant (then continue the task without mentioning the search), or if you already rendered a plugin or skill suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

prompt.description: The initial message for the spawned session. Self-contained — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation. Not shown directly in the UI.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

def investigator(case: CaseFile, team: Team, tab: Tab, deadline: float) -> Agent:
    name = tab.site_id
    system = INVESTIGATOR.format(site=name, url=tab.base_url, brief=case.brief, actions=ACTIONS_HELP)

    def briefing() -> str:
        questions = questions_for_site(name, case.questions())
        news = case.take_news(name)
        text = f"CASE FILE\n{case.status()}\n\nOPEN QUESTIONS\n"
        text += "\n".join(f"- [{qid}] {question}" for qid, question in questions) or "(none)"
        if site_role(name) == "mail" and len(questions) >= 3:
            text += "\n\n" + MAIL_BATCH.format(count=len(questions))
        records = [qid for qid, _ in questions if qid.startswith(("material:", "data:"))]
        if site_role(name) == "erp" and len(records) >= 2:
            text += "\n\n" + RECORD_BATCH.format(count=len(records))
        if news:
            text += "\n\nNEWS FROM YOUR FILED DOCUMENTS\n" + "\n".join(f"- {item}" for item in news)
        own_pending = case.pending_for(name)
        if own_pending:
            text += f"\n\n({own_pending} filed document(s) are still being read.)"
        elif case.pending:
            text += f"\n\n({case.pending} document(s) filed by other agents are still being read.)"
        return text

    agent: Agent
    batched: dict = {}  # kind -> consecutive one-by-one filings, for the file_each nudge (#1)
    worked = [False]  # has filed something: from then on it may go idle by code once its questions are answered

    def finished_here() -> bool:
        """A routed (ERP or mail) agent that has worked and whose website has no open question left and nothing of
        its own still being read: its work is done (its questions are exactly its website's, so nothing is missed)."""
        return (site_role(name) is not None and worked[0] and not case.pending_for(name)
                and not questions_for_site(name, case.questions()))

    async def keep(action: dict) -> str:
        kind = str(action.get("kind", ""))
        document, source = agent.document()
        res = case.file(kind, document, source, name)
        worked[0] = worked[0] or res.startswith("filed")
        if res.startswith("this document is already filed"):
            res += "; do not file this same page again — check OPEN QUESTIONS for what is missing on another page, or finish with done"
        else:
            res += batch_hint(batched, kind, res.startswith("filed"))
        # Fix #2: the bidder Q&A filed as a list that `collect` followed to its own end (over more than one page) is
        # the whole Q&A, so its question closes by itself once it is read (casefile.CaseFile.listed_in_full)
        # instead of keeping the agent browsing until it closes it (run a176359f: 41 s of re-opened documents).
        run = getattr(tab, "last_collect", None)
        if (kind == "clarifications" and res.startswith("filed") and agent.held_by == "collect" and run
                and not run.get("capped") and run.get("pages", 0) >= 2):
            case.listed_in_full["clarifications"] = name
            res += "; this is the Q&A list followed to its end, so the clarifications question closes once it is read"
        return res

    async def file_each_action(action: dict) -> str:
        said = await file_each(tab, action, lambda kind, text, source: case.file(kind, text, source, name),
                               agent.coverage.saw, deadline, agent.page_seen)
        worked[0] = worked[0] or "filed" in said
        # The pages it filed are read in a few seconds. Round-3 run: the ERP agent took a status still being read
        # for "did not parse" and opened the same pages again (3 extra turns); its next turn now sees the facts.
        until = min(deadline, time.time() + FILED_READ_WAIT)
        while case.pending_for(name) and time.time() < until:
            await case.wait_change(case.version, min(1.0, max(0.0, until - time.time())))
        return said + ("\nThe filed pages have been read: their facts are in the case file above."
                       if not case.pending_for(name) else
                       "\nSome filed pages are still being read; their facts follow as news. Do not open them again.")

    async def answer(action: dict) -> str:
        # A completion action can arrive in the same turn as `keep`. Wait for this agent's own
        # extraction result (up to 45 s) instead of blocking on slow extractions from other websites.
        wait_until = min(deadline, time.time() + 45.0)
        while case.pending_for(name) and time.time() < wait_until:
            version = case.version
            if case.pending_for(name):
                await case.wait_change(version, min(1.0, max(0.0, wait_until - time.time())))
        if case.pending_for(name):
            return "Evidence extraction is still pending and the investigation deadline is near; do not repeat this answer action."
        return case.answer(str(action.get("question", "")).strip("[] "), str(action.get("status", "")), str(action.get("note", "")), agent=name)

    # Navigation runs without the model's thinking: about twice as fast. The facts themselves are read by the
    # extraction calls in casefile.py, which keep thinking on. AGENT_THINK=1 turns it back on for comparison.

class Team:
    """Holds an agent that has nothing to do until the case file brings news, and ends the investigation when every
    agent is idle and no filed document is still being read."""

    def __init__(self, case: CaseFile, names: list[str], deadline: float):
        self.case, self.names, self.deadline = case, set(names), deadline
        self.idle: set[str] = set()
        self.finished = asyncio.Event()
        self.woken: dict[str, float] = {}  # when an agent was last woken for finished reading (at most every 30 s)

    def release(self, name: str, candidates: set[str]) -> None:
        """A routed agent (ERP or mail) went idle leaving `candidates` open and nothing is being read any more: those
        go to every agent (RELEASED), and the others are woken by a case-file change. Questions that turn up while it
        is idle are its own work (it is woken for them), so only the ones open when it went idle are candidates."""
        if self.case.pending or site_role(name) is None:
            return
        still = {qid for qid, _ in self.case.questions()} & candidates
        fresh = still - RELEASED
        if fresh:
            RELEASED.update(fresh)
            print(f"[{name}] left open, now offered to every agent: {', '.join(sorted(fresh))}", flush=True)
            bump = getattr(self.case, "_bump", None)
            if bump:
                bump()

    def hook(self, name: str):
        async def hold(why: str) -> str | None:
            before = {qid for qid, _ in questions_for_site(name, self.case.questions())}
            self.release(name, before)
            version = self.case.version
            # Documents still being read when the agent went idle: once one of them is done, the agent is woken if
            # questions are still open. Sandbox run 024bd2ac: the ERP agent went idle "until the requirements are
            # read" with its material questions already open; they were never new, so it slept for 400 s.
            reading = self.case.pending
            self.idle.add(name)
            try:
                while not self.finished.is_set() and time.time() < self.deadline:
                    changed = await self.case.wait_change(version, 1.0)
                    if self.finished.is_set():
                        break
                    if changed:
                        self.release(name, before)
                        version = self.case.version
                        fresh = {qid for qid, _ in questions_for_site(name, self.case.questions())} - before
                        # Fix #2: a routine "your document was read" notice does not wake an idle agent for another
                        # model turn (run 99f03f3f: the tender agent was woken 6 times only to say done again); new
                        # questions and notices that report a problem with its documents still do.
                        if fresh or any(NEEDS_ATTENTION.search(item) for item in self.case.news.get(name) or []):
                            return "The case file has news" + (f"; new open questions: {', '.join(sorted(fresh))}" if fresh else "") + "."
                        still_open = {qid for qid, _ in questions_for_site(name, self.case.questions())}
                        rested = time.time() - self.woken.get(name, 0.0) >= 30
                        if reading and self.case.pending < reading and still_open and rested:
                            self.woken[name] = time.time()
                            return ("Documents that were still being read are now in the case file. Open questions: "
                                    f"{', '.join(sorted(still_open))}. Work on those your website can answer.")
                    elif self.idle == self.names and self.case.pending == 0:
                        self.finished.set()
                return None
            finally:
                self.idle.discard(name)
        return hold

content.text:
Round 7 is ready in the same folder: **`D:\Personal_Projects\QuoteCraft-tier1\starter-kit`** (commit 02d812c on `claude/tier1-speed`, pushed with its Entire checkpoint).

```bash
atira test-run D:/Personal_Projects/QuoteCraft-tier1/starter-kit --challenge rfq
```

**Where run_2e081b8d lost its time (over 6:00):**
- **The mail agent was the bottleneck.** It took 50 turns and 607k input tokens (41% of the run's tokens) and finished last at 4:40. It searched one topic at a time and opened every message by hand: search, unlock the list, open, unlock the text, file.
- **The mail agent kept calling the model after it was done.** It made 4 more model turns after all its questions were already closed, and each one paid for about 12k tokens.
- **The ERP agent sat idle for the first 1:31.** It was waiting for the requirements, because the sites were slow to load at the start (the supplier portal opened 22 s late).
- **What worked:** the ERP batch now gets through (35 turns, down from 53), and the clerk entered all 4 positions in about 28 s.

**Round 7 changes:**

| # | Change | Expected effect |
|---|---|---|
| A | The ERP or mail agent now goes idle without a model call once it has filed something, nothing of its own is still being read, and no question for its site is open. It still wakes up for new questions. | Removes the wasted turns after the work is done |
| B | When the mail agent has 3 or more open questions, it is told to do one broad search per folder, unlock the list once, then file all the records in one batch. | Mail agent drops from about 50 turns to about 15–20 |
| C | The ERP agent is told to go through one record completely (stock and price scales included) before batching, so the batch can repeat every click. | Fewer stock and price steps done by hand |

The price and discount calculation, how the RFQ is read, reconciliation and the pre-submit checks are unchanged. The fair-play scan of the new lines found no hardcoded scenario values. The model still chooses what to search for and what to file.

I only checked that the code parses; I didn't run it or the unit tests, as you asked. My estimate is about 4:00–4:45 and roughly 30% lower cost, but your test run is the real check. Round 7 has its own section in `BEST_RUN_TIMING.md`, with an empty row waiting for this run's result.

The tracked log `logs (2).jsonl` is missing from the worktree root. I left that deletion out of the commit.

content.text:
No. The bid page doesn't go back to the other websites for data. It types everything from memory. I checked the bid phase of run_2e081b8d (04:41 to 06:20):

**What happens when the tender form opens**
1. **04:41:** the investigation ends and the bid is calculated in memory: all 5 positions, prices, the 5% discount and the 356,949.62 total. This is the `BID: {...}` line in the log.
2. **04:41 to 06:01:** the clerk works only on the tender portal, typing straight from that bid: company, VAT number, email, the positions (4 of them filled in one action), discount and total.
3. **During the whole bid phase the customer portal and ERP browsers got zero inputs.** Nobody re-reads them.

**The one other website it does touch is the mailbox, and that's required:**
- **06:01:** the clerk clicks "TAN anfordern" (request TAN). The portal then emails a one-time code that didn't exist before that click, so it can't be in memory. Old codes in the mailbox are traps.
- **06:03 to 06:14:** the courier opens the mailbox, passes its robot check, reloads and reads the newest code. That's 3 model turns and about 13 s.
- When the bid phase starts, the code also opens a fresh tab in the mail browser in the background, with no model call, so the mailbox is already loaded when the code is needed. That's probably the "website opening again" you saw. It isn't fetching any data.

**Where the bid phase's 99 s actually go**

| Step | Time | Could it be cut? |
|---|---|---|
| Reaching the form (starts on the Q&A page, then goes to the overview, then to the bid form) | ~9 s, 2 turns | Slightly: start on the tender's main page |
| First position by hand: the "keine" certification option didn't exist, so the model retried with "Ohne Zertifizierung" | ~19 s, 2 turns | Some: one turn instead of two |
| 4 positions in one action | ~28 s, browser time only | Some: shorter waits between steps |
| Conditions, declarations, TAN request | ~11 s, 3 turns | Little |
| Courier gets the TAN | ~13 s, 3 turns | No: the robot check stays with the model under fair play |
| Enter the TAN, check, submit | ~6 s, 2 turns | No |

So at most about 15–20 s could come out of the bid phase. The big waste was the investigation (280 s), and mostly the mail agent's 50 turns, which round 7 targets.

Two runs are going right now (run_c84d7128 and run_ddfa36f5). If one of them is round 7, send me its log when it finishes. If you also want the small bid-phase trims, I can add them as round 8.

content.text:
Round 7 (run_ddfa36f5) scored **100 in 5:10 for $0.138**. Round 6 took 6:19 and $0.161. The mail agent dropped from 50 turns to 27, so the **ERP agent is now what decides when the bid can start**.

**The whole run (5:10)**

| Phase | Run clock | Time | Model turns |
|---|---|---|---|
| Read the brief | 0:00–0:04 | 4 s | 1 |
| **Investigation (4 agents at once)** | 0:04–3:20 | **197 s** | 89 |
| Fill the bid form | 3:20–4:51 | **91 s** | 15 |
| Get the TAN from the mailbox | 4:51–5:05 | 14 s | 5 |
| Enter the TAN and submit | 5:05–5:10 | 4 s | 1 |

**Investigation, per agent**

| Agent | Turns | Working | Idle | Tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tender portal | 11 | 0:04–0:48 | – | 111k |
| Customer portal | 13 | 0:04–0:54 | – | 118k |
| Mail | 27 (was 50) | 0:04–2:35 | 0:16–0:42 | 314k (was 607k) |
| **ERP (finishes last)** | 38 | 0:04–3:19 | 0:13–0:42 | 378k |

**ERP agent, step by step**

| Stretch | Time | Turns | Waste |
|---|---|---|---|
| Log in and pass the access check | 9 s | 2 | – |
| Idle until the requirements are read (it needs the catalogue groups) | 30 s | 0 | **~30 s**: it could learn the record layout meanwhile |
| Find the material search (the F4 link didn't work) | 11 s | 4 | ~7 s |
| Learn one record all the way, by hand | 43 s | 14 | needed once |
| **Walk a second record fully by hand, then file it again in a batch** | 45 s | 11 | **~35 s** |
| 3 searches and 3 batches (5 records) | 68 s | 6 | the browser needs ~9 s per record |

**Bid form, step by step**

| Step | Time | Turns | Waste |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reach the bid form | 11 s | 2 | ~5 s |
| Bidder data and offer type | 6 s | 2 | – |
| **First position by hand** | 31 s | 6 | **~20 s**: round 6 needed only 2 turns |
| The other 4 positions in one action | 32 s | 1 | browser time, ~7 s per position |
| Conditions, declarations, check, TAN request | 11 s | 4 | – |
| Mailbox agent gets the TAN | 14 s | 5 | – (robot checks stay with the model) |

**What's left to cut (round 8 candidates)**
1. **~35 s:** the ERP agent walked a second record by hand after it had already learned the clicks.
2. **~30 s:** the ERP agent sits idle at the start. It could learn the record layout while waiting.
3. **~20 s:** the first bid position should take 1–2 turns, not 6.
4. **Part of ~75 s:** the fixed browser waits inside the batch filing and the position entry could be shorter.

content.content:
public tender and a calculator has priced it: the BID SHEET below is the final result. You work the tender portal
"{site}" at {url} in your own browser tab, and your whole job is to get exactly this bid into the portal's bid
form, sign it, submit it and read the confirmation. You do not research and you do not recalculate.

TASK BRIEF (background on what a valid submission is; the values to enter come from the bid sheet)
{brief}
END OF BRIEF

BIDDER
{bidder}

BID SHEET
{sheet}

Reading the bid sheet
- "decision" is "bid" or "no_bid". A no_bid has no positions and a total of zero: take the form's way of
  declining, and still sign and submit it.
- "positions" has one entry per tender position that is offered. Enter each under its own position number.
- "material" describes the offered product, for forms that make you pick or configure it: choose what equals
  these values.
- Amounts are net EUR, written here with a decimal point and without thousands separators. A field may expect
  another notation (a decimal comma, a unit, whole numbers for weeks and pieces): follow its hints, placeholder
  and error messages. Change the notation only, never the value.
- null means the value is not known: leave that field empty. 0 or 0.00 is a known zero: enter it.
- "omitted_positions" could not be priced. Never invent values for them: use the form's explicit way of leaving
  a position out, if it has one.
- Save turns: once you have seen how one step of the form works (which fields, which button applies a choice or
  moves on), do a whole step in one "steps" action, using the labels exactly as the page shows them. If it stops
  part-way, read the page and carry on from there. You know every value from the bid; you do not need to see each
  list first.
- POSITIONS: enter the FIRST position the form asks for yourself, with "steps" actions, and read the result: learn
  which choices exist (e.g. how the form names "no certificate") and which control SAVES a position and moves on to
  the next one. A control that only adds another, empty line ("add position") does not save the one you filled;
  pressing it can put the form out of step. Once the first position is saved and the form shows the next one,
  enter ALL remaining positions with ONE enter_positions action (described below) whose template repeats exactly
  the steps that worked, with placeholders for the values, ending with that saving control. Code repeats it for
  each position the form asks for, in the form's own order. The form may start with any position and use its own
  order: enter the one it shows; do not go back to look for the lowest number first.
- A position is entered once. When the form saves it, it may list it, show a short confirmation and empty its
  fields for a further line: then go on with the control that moves to the next position or step, and do not
  enter the same position again.

{actions}
One more action:
  {{"do": "ask_mail", "task": "<what you need and how to recognise it>"}}
      A colleague who has the bidder's mailbox open in another browser looks for it and answers. This is how you
      get the signing code (TAN) the portal sends by mail. Ask only after you have triggered the code in the
      portal, and pass on what you know about it (the tender reference, that you requested it just now, anything
      the portal displayed about it): the mailbox also holds older codes that no longer work.
  {{"do": "enter_positions", "decimal": ",", "steps": [{{"field": "<label>", "value": "{{bore_mm}}"}},
      {{"press": "<apply button>"}}, {{"field": "<label>", "value": "{{certification}}", "if_null": "<the option for none>"}},
      {{"press": "<apply button>"}}, {{"field": "<label>", "value": "{{material_number}}"}},
      {{"field": "<label>", "value": "{{quantity}}"}}, {{"field": "<label>", "value": "{{unit_price}}"}},
      {{"press": "<button that saves the position and moves on>"}}]}}
      Enters the bid sheet's positions with one template, written like a "steps" chain with the labels exactly as the
      page shows them. A value may hold placeholders of a position's bid-sheet values: {{position}},
      {{material_number}}, {{quantity}}, {{unit_price}}, {{lead_time_weeks}}, {{base_unit_price}},
      {{surcharge_per_unit}}, {{packaging_per_unit}}, {{rebate_total}}, {{bore_mm}}, {{stroke_mm}}, {{pressure_bar}},
      {{mounting}}, {{certification}}. "decimal" is the decimal sign the form's amount fields take. A placeholder whose
      value is null leaves that step out, unless the step says what the form takes instead ("if_null", e.g. the
      option for "no certificate"). Without "positions", every position the form shows is entered one after the
      other until it shows none that is not entered yet; a template that chooses {{position}} itself goes through the
      bid sheet in order. "positions": ["<position>"] enters just those. It stops at the first step that does not
      work and says where; then read the page, fix that, and call it again (the template is remembered: {{"do":
      "enter_positions"}} goes on with the positions not entered yet).
  {{"do": "check_submission"}}
      Read the current review page and produce a no-model checklist of visible errors, unfilled required controls,
      tender reference, offered positions and total. Run this immediately before the irreversible final step.
      BLOCKER is something the page shows to be wrong. NOT SHOWN is something a review must show and this page
      does not: a page that does not show the bid proves nothing about what the portal holds.
  {{"do": "finalize", "id": 12}}
      Press the final submit/confirm control only after check_submission reported READY. Never use ordinary click for
      the irreversible final submit control.

How to work
- Start from the page you are on and find the bid form of tender {reference}. Log in again if the portal asks.
- A bid form asks, in an order of its own, for things like the bidder's details, bid or no bid, the positions,
  the commercial terms, declarations, a review and a signature. Read each page and give it what it asks for,

    async def select(self, aid, value: str) -> str:
        locator = self._locator(aid)
        if locator is None or await locator.count() == 0:
            return f"there is no element [{aid}] on the page any more"
        wanted = str(value)
        for attempt in ({"value": wanted}, {"label": wanted}):
            try:
                await locator.select_option(timeout=2000, **attempt)
                await self.settle()
                if await self._modal_is_open():
                    return "the page now has a modal dialog; read it before acting behind it"
                return f'selected "{wanted}" in [{aid}]'
            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
                continue
        options = await locator.evaluate("el => [...(el.options || [])].map(o => o.value + '=' + o.textContent.trim())")
        loose = [o.split("=", 1)[0] for o in options if wanted.lower() in o.lower()]
        if len(loose) == 1:
            await locator.select_option(value=loose[0])
            await self.settle()
            return f'selected "{loose[0]}" in [{aid}]'
        return f'[{aid}] has no option "{wanted}"; options: {"; ".join(options)[:600]}'

    async def set(self, aid, value) -> str:
        locator = self._locator(aid)
        if locator is None or await locator.count() == 0:
            return f"there is no element [{aid}] on the page any more"
        info = await self._describe(locator)
        if info["disabled"]:
            return f"[{aid}] is disabled; nothing happened"
        try:
            if info["type"] in ("checkbox", "radio"):
                wanted = bool(value)
                try:
                    await locator.set_checked(wanted, timeout=1500)
                except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001  covered or restyled: toggle it as its label would
                    if await locator.is_checked() != wanted:
                        await locator.evaluate("el => el.click()")
                if await locator.is_checked() != wanted:
                    return f"[{aid}] did not change; it is still {'unchecked' if wanted else 'checked'}"
            else:  # a slider or another input whose value is set in one go

    async def settle(self):
        """Wait until the page, its frames and the data they fetch have arrived and nothing more is on its way."""
        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
        end, quiet = loop.time() + SETTLE_SECONDS, None
        await asyncio.sleep(0.1)  # let a click start its request
        while loop.time() < end:

async def select(self, aid, value: str) -> str:
        locator = self._locator(aid)
        if locator is None or await locator.count() == 0:
            return f"there is no element [{aid}] on the page any more"
        wanted = str(value)
        for attempt in ({"value": wanted}, {"label": wanted}):
            try:
                await locator.select_option(timeout=2000, **attempt)
                await self.settle()
                if await self._modal_is_open():
                    return "the page now has a modal dialog; read it before acting behind it"
                return f'selected "{wanted}" in [{aid}]'
            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
                continue
        options = await locator.evaluate("el => [...(el.options || [])].map(o => o.value + '=' + o.textContent.trim())")
        loose = [o.split("=", 1)[0] for o in options if wanted.lower() in o.lower()]
        if len(loose) == 1:
            await locator.select_option(value=loose[0])
            await self.settle()
            return f'selected "{loose[0]}" in [{aid}]'
        return f'[{aid}] has no option "{wanted}"; options: {"; ".join(options)[:600]}'

name = tab.site_id
    system = INVESTIGATOR.format(site=name, url=tab.base_url, brief=case.brief, actions=ACTIONS_HELP)

    def briefing() -> str:
        questions = questions_for_site(name, case.questions())
        news = case.take_news(name)
        text = f"CASE FILE\n{case.status()}\n\nOPEN QUESTIONS\n"
        text += "\n".join(f"- [{qid}] {question}" for qid, question in questions) or "(none)"
        if site_role(name) == "mail" and len(questions) >= 3:
            text += "\n\n" + MAIL_BATCH.format(count=len(questions))
        records = [qid for qid, _ in questions if qid.startswith(("material:", "data:"))]
        if site_role(name) == "erp" and records and learned[0]:
            text += "\n\n" + RECORD_LEARNED
        elif site_role(name) == "erp" and len(records) >= 2:
            text += "\n\n" + RECORD_BATCH.format(count=len(records))
        elif site_role(name) == "erp" and not questions and not worked[0]:
            text += "\n\n" + ERP_PREPARE
        if news:
            text += "\n\nNEWS FROM YOUR FILED DOCUMENTS\n" + "\n".join(f"- {item}" for item in news)
        own_pending = case.pending_for(name)
        if own_pending:
            text += f"\n\n({own_pending} filed document(s) are still being read.)"
        elif case.pending:
            text += f"\n\n({case.pending} document(s) filed by other agents are still being read.)"
        return text

    agent: Agent
    batched: dict = {}  # kind -> consecutive one-by-one filings, for the file_each nudge (#1)
    worked = [False]  # has filed something: from then on it may go idle by code once its questions are answered
    learned = [False]  # has filed a price page reached through a record: the record layout is known (RECORD_LEARNED)

    def finished_here() -> bool:
        """A routed (ERP or mail) agent that has worked and whose website has no open question left and nothing of
        its own still being read: its work is done (its questions are exactly its website's, so nothing is missed)."""
        return (site_role(name) is not None and worked[0] and not case.pending_for(name)
                and not questions_for_site(name, case.questions()))

    async def keep(action: dict) -> str:
        kind = str(action.get("kind", ""))
        document, source = agent.document()
        res = case.file(kind, document, source, name)
        worked[0] = worked[0] or res.startswith("filed")
        if res.startswith("this document is already filed"):
            res += "; do not file this same page again — check OPEN QUESTIONS for what is missing on another page, or finish with done"
        else:
            res += batch_hint(batched, kind, res.startswith("filed"))
        if kind == "price_conditions" and res.startswith("filed") and not learned[0]:
            learned[0] = True
            res += ("; you now know the record layout: file every further candidate with file_each from its result "
                    "list, repeating your tabs and click paths, and do not walk another record by hand")
